summary: This is Emil Kowalski's ask-sonner agent skill: a working guide to Sonner, his React toast library, covering setup, which toast() call to use, common recipes, styling and troubleshooting. Setup is exactly two pieces: one <Toaster /> mounted once near the root, and toast() called only from client code. It gives a styling escalation ladder (defaults, inline styles, classes with !important, then headless toast.custom()) and recommends the headless rung, wrapped in your own toast() abstraction, for a design-system toast. A troubleshooting table maps the usual failures (toasts missing, doubled, unstyled, behind modals, ignoring dark mode, never closing) to their causes and fixes. For a design system it defines how a toast component should be wired, themed and customised without fighting the library.
key_ideas: A toast system needs one Toaster mounted once at the root and a toast() function called from client code; nothing else.
A second mounted Toaster duplicates every toast, so the Toaster must never be per-page or conditional.
toast() does nothing on the server: a server action returns its result and the client shows the toast.
Pick the call by intent: plain, typed status, loading updated by id, promise-driven, with an action button, custom JSX in the default shell, or fully headless.
Updating a toast means calling toast() again with the same id; only the props you pass change, and a typed call switches the type.
Styling is a ladder: defaults, inline styles, classes on parts, then headless. Climb only as far as needed; jumping straight to the top rung is fine, lingering in the middle is not.
For a design-system toast, go headless with toast.custom() and wrap it in your own toast() abstraction, keeping Sonner's positioning, stacking and swipe.
Classes on toast parts need !important because Sonner's injected styles win the cascade; needing many of them is the signal to go headless.
The toast theme defaults to light and does not follow the OS; it must be set to 'system' or fed the app's resolved theme.
There is no single 'closed' callback: onDismiss covers the close button and swipes, onAutoClose covers the timeout.
Toasts hidden behind modals come from stacking contexts or z-index; the fix is mounting the Toaster at the document root outside dialogs and portals.
Lost styles in Astro, view transitions or Shadow DOM are fixed by importing the stylesheet explicitly or copying the style tag into the shadow root.
With several toasters, untargeted toasts render in every one; give each Toaster an id and target it with toasterId.
Mobile needs a smaller edge distance: offset defaults to 32px and mobileOffset to 16px below 600px.

rules.rule: Mount one <Toaster /> once, as close to the root as possible (several toasters are a separate recipe, each with its own id).
rules.why: Setup is two pieces, and only two; a second mounted Toaster duplicates every toast.
rules.evidence: One `<Toaster />`, mounted once**, as close to the root as possible

rules.rule: In Next.js, put the Toaster in layout.tsx.
rules.why: It belongs as close to the root as possible and works inside server components.

rules.rule: Never render the Toaster per page or conditionally.
rules.why: A second mounted Toaster duplicates every toast, and an unmounted one means toasts never appear.
rules.evidence: Never render it per-page or conditionally

rules.rule: Call toast() only from client code (event handlers, effects, callbacks); it is a plain function, so no hook or provider is needed.
rules.why: It is a plain function that does nothing on the server.

rules.rule: Do not call toast() inside a server action; return the result and call toast() in the client code that receives it.
rules.why: toast() is client-only and does nothing on the server.
rules.evidence: in a server action, return the result

rules.rule: Import Toaster once, in the layout, and import toast wherever client code needs it.
rules.why: Setup is exactly these two imports.

rules.rule: For a plain message use toast('Title') and add { description } for a second line.
rules.why: This is the call the source maps to a plain message.

rules.rule: For success, error, info or warning messages use the typed calls toast.success, toast.error, toast.info and toast.warning.
rules.why: They carry the matching status icon.

rules.rule: When you manage the async state yourself, show toast.loading('…') and then update that toast by its id.
rules.why: It shows a spinner and changes in place when updated by id.
rules.evidence: Spinner while you manage state yourself

rules.rule: When the loading, success and error states are tied to one promise, use toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error }), passing functions to success and error to use the resolved value or the error.
rules.why: success and error accept functions receiving the resolved value or error.
rules.evidence: Loading → success/error tied to a promise

rules.rule: Give a toast a button that does something with { action: { label, onClick } }, use cancel for the secondary button, and call event.preventDefault() in onClick to keep the toast open.
rules.why: The action closes the toast unless onClick calls event.preventDefault(); cancel is the secondary variant.

rules.rule: Put custom JSX inside the default toast shell with toast(<jsx />).
rules.why: This keeps Sonner's default shell around your content.

rules.rule: For custom JSX with no default styles at all, use toast.custom((t) => <jsx />) and use t's id to dismiss it.
rules.why: It is headless, and t gives you the id to dismiss.
rules.evidence: Custom JSX, no styles at all

rules.rule: Update a toast by calling toast() again with the same id, passing only the props that change; switch its type with a typed call such as toast.success(…, { id }).
rules.why: Only the props you pass change, and a typed call changes the type; this is how loading to success works without toast.promise.
rules.evidence: call `toast()` again with the same `id`; only the props you pass change

rules.rule: Persist a toast with { duration: Infinity }.
rules.why: This is the source's recipe for persisting.

rules.rule: Dismiss one toast with toast.dismiss(id) and all toasts with toast.dismiss().
rules.why: This is the source's dismiss recipe.

rules.rule: Read active toasts with useSonner() in React and toast.getActiveToasts() outside it.
rules.why: This is the source's recipe for reading active toasts.

rules.rule: To put links or components in a toast's title or description, pass a function that returns the JSX.
rules.why: The source gives this as the way to render links or components in the text.
rules.evidence: Links or components in the text

rules.rule: With more than one Toaster, give each an id and target it with toasterId in every toast() call.
rules.why: Without toasterId, every toaster renders the toast.
rules.evidence: Without `toasterId`, every toaster renders the toast

rules.rule: Handle onDismiss and onAutoClose separately, and wire both when you need to react to every way a toast closes.
rules.why: onDismiss fires on close button or swipe and onAutoClose on timeout; there is no single closed callback [wiring both is inferred].
rules.evidence: They are separate; there is no single "closed" callback

rules.rule: Climb the styling ladder (defaults, inline style, classNames, headless) only as far as the change requires; jumping straight to headless is fine.
rules.why: Jumping to the top rung too early is fine (it is the recommended end state), but lingering in the middle rungs is not.
rules.evidence: Climb only as far as the change requires

rules.rule: Do not settle on the middle styling rungs (inline styles or !important classes) as the long-term setup.
rules.why: The top rung is the recommended end state; lingering in the middle is not fine.
rules.evidence: lingering in the middle is not

rules.rule: Start from the defaults, adding richColors on the Toaster for colorful success and error, and invert to flip toasts against the theme.
rules.why: This is rung 1 of the ladder.
rules.evidence: plus `richColors` on the Toaster for colorful success/error, `invert` to flip against the theme

rules.rule: For small tweaks, use toastOptions={{ style: {…} }} on the Toaster for all toasts, or style on a single toast() call.
rules.why: This is rung 2, inline tweaks.

rules.rule: When styling toast parts with classNames (toast, title, description, actionButton, cancelButton, closeButton), mark every class !important; in Tailwind use the ! prefix.
rules.why: Sonner's injected styles win the cascade.
rules.evidence: Sonner's injected styles win the cascade

rules.rule: Once more than a few classes need !important, stop and go headless.
rules.why: That is the signal the middle rung is being over-used.
rules.evidence: If you're marking more than a few things important, stop

rules.rule: Build the design-system toast headless with toast.custom() and your own JSX, and wrap it in your own toast() abstraction.
rules.why: Headless keeps Sonner's positioning, stacking and swipe, and it is the recommended approach for a design-system toast.
rules.evidence: The recommended approach for a design-system toast: wrap it in your own `toast()` abstraction

rules.rule: Prefer headless toast.custom() over unstyled: true.
rules.why: unstyled is a halfway house; headless gives more control for the same effort.

rules.rule: Swap icons per type with the Toaster's icons prop, per toast with icon, and remove one with null.
rules.why: These are the three icon controls the source lists.
rules.evidence: swap defaults per-type with the Toaster's `icons` prop, per-toast with `icon`, remove with `null`

rules.rule: Set the Toaster theme to 'system' or pass your theme provider's resolved theme, e.g. <Toaster theme={resolvedTheme} /> from next-themes.
rules.why: theme defaults to 'light' and does not track the OS, so dark mode is otherwise ignored.

rules.rule: If a toast never appears, check that a Toaster is mounted at the root and not unmounted by a conditional render or per-page placement, and that toast() runs on the client.
rules.why: Missing or unmounted Toasters and server-side calls are the listed causes.

rules.rule: Do not mount a Toaster in both the layout and a page; keep one.
rules.why: Two mounted Toasters make the same toast appear twice.

rules.rule: Fire toasts from event handlers rather than effects, or pass a stable id when a toast must fire from an effect.
rules.why: React StrictMode's dev double-invoke runs effects twice; a stable id makes the second call update rather than duplicate.

rules.rule: When toasts render completely unstyled (common in Astro and with view transitions), import the stylesheet explicitly in a layout.
rules.why: Sonner's injected stylesheet was lost.

rules.rule: Inside Shadow DOM, copy the style tag whose text includes [data-sonner-toaster] into the shadow root.
rules.why: Sonner's styles land in document.head, not the shadow root.

rules.rule: Mount the Toaster at the document root, outside any dialog or portal container, so toasts are not hidden behind modals or clipped.
rules.why: An ancestor with transform, filter or overflow creates a stacking context, or the overlay out-z-indexes the toaster.
rules.evidence: Move `<Toaster />` to the document root, outside any dialog/portal container

rules.rule: Do not place the Toaster inside an element that uses transform, filter or overflow [inferred].
rules.why: Those create a stacking context that hides or clips toasts [phrased as a don't: inferred from the cause column].
rules.evidence: An ancestor creates a stacking context

rules.rule: Add richColors to the Toaster when success and error must look green and red.
rules.why: Gray success and error toasts are the default.

rules.rule: If a toast never closes, check for duration: Infinity, dismissible: false, or a toast.promise whose promise never settles.
rules.why: Each makes the toast stay; an unsettled promise leaves the loading toast waiting forever.

rules.rule: Pass toast.promise a promise, or a function returning one, that actually resolves or rejects.
rules.why: Otherwise toast.promise stays stuck on loading.

rules.rule: If swipe-to-dismiss goes the wrong way or does not work, override swipeDirections on the Toaster.
rules.why: Swipe directions derive from position.

rules.rule: Keep toasts off the screen edge with offset on desktop (default 32px) and mobileOffset below 600px (default 16px), as numbers, CSS strings or per-side objects.
rules.why: These are the settings for toasts that sit too close to the edge on mobile.
rules.evidence: Toasts too close to the screen edge on mobile

rules.rule: Answer Sonner tasks from the skill first, and read API.md when an exact prop name, type or default is needed.
rules.why: The skill says to answer from this file first and keep full prop tables in API.md.

rules.rule: When Tailwind or CSS classes on toasts have no effect, mark them !important or move to unstyled or headless.
rules.why: Sonner's default styles override the classes.
rules.evidence: Default styles override them. Mark them `!important`, or use `unstyled` / headless

caveats: This is an agent skill prompt, pinned to commit 85e8e23 of emilkowalski/skills; Sonner's API and defaults can change.
The skill tells the agent to open with a fixed line and say nothing more until asked; that line is self-description, not design guidance.
Framework-specific fixes (Next.js layout.tsx, next-themes, Astro, Tailwind ! prefix) apply only to those stacks.
React-only: rules about Toaster, toast() and hooks do not transfer as code to iOS, Android or desktop toolkits.
